**Finding submitted: deviation (Section 14.2, ¶p0054).**

- **Issue:** Vendor takes exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created for us, leaving us only a revocable, non-transferable licence limited to the Order Form term. That fails the preferred position (Customer ownership with Vendor assignment) *and* the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense).
- **Why 14.3/13.2 don't cure it:** the perpetual licence in 13.2 reaches only Vendor Technology delivered paid-up or embedded in a Deliverable — not the Deliverables themselves. The term-limited, revocable licence also conflicts with 10.1 (rights in accepted Deliverables continue) and 10.2/6.2 (we pay for Deliverables).
- **Compliant elsewhere, noted not flagged:** 14.1 (Customer owns Customer Data, pre-existing IP), 14.3 (Vendor Technology retention with identification duty), 14.4 (no joint ownership; feedback rights preserved), 15.1 (no model training on Customer Data).
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** reverses the assignment so we own Deliverables, while expressly preserving Vendor's background IP under 14.3 and the Section 13.2 perpetual licence for embedded Vendor Technology. Fallback offered in the comment if Vendor cannot assign.
